name: Smarty Discounts
summary: Shopify discount engine for the rules the native one cannot express: capped and fixed-amount discounts that hold up across currencies, tiers by quantity, subtotal or weight, BXGY, gifts and mix-and-match, targeted by product, customer, cart, market, country or company. Each tier includes two discounts at the level above. Launched January 2025, six reviews as of 4 Sep 2026.
best_for: Shopify merchants whose promotions have outgrown the native discount engine: capped amounts, a fixed amount that behaves correctly in several currencies, tiers by quantity, subtotal or weight, BXGY, gifts, mix-and-match, and who want to build them with rules rather than with a developer, targeting by product, customer, cart, market, country or company
skip_if: your promotions are ordinary percentage or fixed-amount codes, which Shopify's built-in discounts already do for free; or you want a long support and reliability record before a young app gets write access to the discounts in your checkout
honest_knock: The evidence base is thin. The app launched on 14 January 2025 and carried six reviews on 4 September 2026, all five stars; on 11 October 2026 the listing still shows six, five at five stars and one at four, and six is not a track record, and the vendor, Neezon, is a small developer in Ho Chi Minh City rather than a company with a support contract behind it. The listing is unusually candid about what that means at the bottom of the ladder: the free plan's own feature list says low support. Add to that what the app needs to do its job. The data-access panel says it reads customer data flagged as sensitive and can view and edit customers, products, discounts and the Online Store, which is the access any discount engine needs but is still broad. And because the ladder gates discount types rather than volume, the plan you land on is decided by the one rule you cannot live without: if the campaign you have in mind needs time-period scheduling or free shipping on a single rule, you are on Pro at $25.99 regardless of how few discounts you run.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month or $99.99 a year (17% off vs monthly)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/smarty-discount) Three tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Forever Free costs nothing, Lite is $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, and Pro is $25.99 a month or $259.99 a year; the annual price on both paid tiers saves 17%, and both carry a 7-day free trial. What you are buying is capability, not volume: there is no order cap, no revenue meter and no surcharge tied to your Shopify plan anywhere in the block. Free covers product and order discounts with basic targeting and what the listing itself calls low support. Lite adds shipping and mix-and-match discounts, enhanced targeting and priority support. Pro includes every discount type, every targeting rule, active time periods and free shipping on a single rule. One detail in the plan table is worth reading twice, because it is unusual and it is in your favour: each tier gives unlimited discounts at its own level plus up to two at the level above. On Free you can build two Lite-grade discounts, on Lite two Pro-grade ones. That is a working trial of the next tier rather than a locked door, and it means you can prove the rule you actually need before you pay for it. Re-verified 11 October 2026 on apps.shopify.com/smarty-discount: the three tiers, both prices, the 17% saving and the 7-day trials are unchanged. The vendor's plans page (neezon.com/docs/smarty-discounts/plans, read the same day) adds the gates the listing leaves out: shipping and mix-and-match need Lite, while Buy X Get Y, Combine and discount code rejection need Pro; bulk code generations are capped at one on Free and five on Lite; multi-currency is not on Free, 'compare in multi-currency' on Lite and full on Pro. The same page says the in-app Billing page can show promo, coupon or legacy pricing and is the source of truth for the price your shop sees.

free_plan_evidence: The listing is unusually candid about what that means at the bottom of the ladder: the free plan's own feature list says low support.

compare_with.name: Shopify's own native discounts
compare_with.why: the honest comparison is not another app but the discount engine already sitting in your admin. Shopify does percentage, fixed-amount, buy-X-get-Y and free-shipping discounts at no cost, and for most stores that is enough. Smarty Discounts starts earning its $9.99 or $25.99 at the point where you need a cap on the discount, a fixed amount that converts properly across markets, tiers built on weight or subtotal rather than quantity, or targeting by company or market: the rules the native engine cannot express at all

claims.claim: Shopify merchants with promotions beyond basic codes
claims.observed: A volume discount with two quantity tiers (10 percent from 2 pieces, 20 percent from 4) was made as an automatic percentage discount on all products and showed Active; the dollar cap and tiers by weight were not tried.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier audience for promotions beyond basic codes versus one quantity tier discount; cap and weight tiers were not opened.
claims.buying_consequence: The kind of rule beyond a basic code can be made, but the capped and weight based rules of the dossier were not tested.

claims.claim: This discount is automatically applied at checkout.
claims.observed: The app and Shopify show the discount as Active, Automatic, Used 0. We did not run a cart through the store, because the store has a password, so the discount was never seen at work.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: App wording on automatic application at checkout versus a status Active with Used 0 and no cart.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether the tiers take the right amount off a real cart is not known from this test.

claims.claim: Stores running dated campaigns or gift offers
claims.observed: Active with time periods is greyed out on the Free plan and Buy X Get Y is marked as needing test mode or Pro; neither was tried and no paid plan was started.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier audience for dated campaigns versus features that are greyed out on Free and were not opened.
claims.buying_consequence: Dated campaigns and gift offers could not be tested on the Free plan.

claims.claim: Owners wary of a young app touching checkout
claims.observed: The app asked to view customer data and staff data and to view and edit store data, the listing shows 5.0 from 6 reviews, and one discount was made without any problem; no cart or checkout was run through it.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier audience for a young app versus one saved discount and an install screen; no checkout was tried.
claims.buying_consequence: How the app behaves in a live checkout during a sale was not seen.

claims.observed: The app shows Free, Pro at $9.99 a month with unlimited discount rules, all discount types and a 7 day trial, and Custom at $99 a month. The dossier lists Lite at $9.99 and Pro at $25.99 and says Buy X Get Y and active time periods are only on the top tier; the app showed no Lite and no Pro at $25.99.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier plan names and prices versus the three plan columns of the Billing page on a Basic store.
claims.buying_consequence: On a Shopify Basic store the single paid plan costs $9.99 and lists all discount types, which is cheaper than the $25.99 top tier in the dossier.

claims.observed: The listing gives the prices by Shopify plan: $9.99 for Basic, $15.99 for Grow, $19.99 for Advanced and $25.99 for Plus a month. Our store is on Basic, so only $9.99 was seen in the app and the other prices were read from the listing only.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier flat plan prices versus a listing with prices by Shopify plan that could not be seen in the app.
claims.buying_consequence: The monthly price may depend on the Shopify plan of the store, which the dossier does not say; larger stores may pay more.

claims.observed: The Free plan lists 2 discount rules and 1 bulk code generation; after one rule the app said that 1 Free-tier discount remains.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier free tier versus the Free column and the remaining count message in the app.
claims.buying_consequence: The free plan is limited to 2 discount rules, so a third rule needs the paid plan.

claims.observed: The Custom plan costs $99 a month and a custom rule build is $120 an hour with no estimate, typically 6 to 10 hours per rule; the Contact button was not pressed and the plan was not tested.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Plan page wording on custom builds versus a plan that was not tried and a button that was not pressed.
claims.buying_consequence: A custom rule at that rate is roughly $720 to $1,200 on top of the monthly fee, which could not be checked.

claims.observed: The Shopify approval screen for Pro shows $9,99 USD every 30 days with a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov and a total of $9,99 due 24 Nov plus any applicable taxes. The plan is called Pro Basic. We cancelled the screen and nothing was approved.
claims.plan: Pro approval screen, cancelled, development store
claims.comparability: Plan page Pro price versus the approval screen amount; no stored cost rule was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: The monthly price of $9.99 matches the plan page before taxes and the first bill comes after the 7-day trial.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Smarty Discounts on a Shopify development store: the install, one automatic volume discount made in the app (Active in the app and in Shopify, not tried in a cart), the plans in the listing and in the app, the Shopify approval screen for Pro (cancelled), and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no theme change was made. Install: the App Store listing (English) is Smarty Discounts by Neezon, rated 5.0 from 6 reviews, with the line Free plan available. Free trial available. The install form was submitted at 15:33:34 and the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked. The app (version 2.7.1) opened straight on the Free plan without a plan or approval screen; a welcome dialog Welcome to Smarty Discounts with 4 steps was dismissed. No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. Core action, a volume discount on products: Create discount, Amount off product, the method Automatic discount, the title Snowboard volume deal, Percentage, Add tier gave Volume-based on Quantity with Tier 1 (Quantity 2, Get 10.0 %) and Add another tier gave Tier 2 (Quantity 4, Get 20.0 %); both are default values and were not changed. Applies to All products. Save gave the message Snowboard volume deal was created successfully with This discount is automatically applied at checkout and the status Active; the summary card says 2 volume-based tiers up to 20% off and the app says You have 1 Free-tier discounts remaining on your plan. Shopify Discounts shows the discount as Active, Automatic, All customers, Amount off product, Used 0. The dashboard of the app counts 1 automatic product discount and 9 from other apps or Shopify itself. The discount was not seen in a cart or checkout, because the store has a password and we did not run a cart through it; only the status Active in the app and in Shopify was confirmed. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install at 15:33:34 to the saved discount (about 15:35), in about 9 clicks and steps. Plans in the listing: Free (2 discount rules); Shopify Basic $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year; Shopify Grow $15.99 a month or $159.99 a year (Advanced $19.99 or $199.99); Shopify Plus $25.99 a month or $259.99 a year; a 7-day free trial; all charges are billed in USD. Plans in the app (Billing): Free with 2 discount rules, 1 bulk code generation and email support (greyed out items: Single code/rule free shipping, Active with time periods, Early access to features); Pro at $9.99 a month, marked Most popular, with Includes 7 day trial, Unlimited discount rules, All discounts types and priority support; Custom at $99 a month, where a custom rule build costs $120 an hour with no estimate (typically 6 to 10 hours per rule, so roughly $720 to $1,200 per rule at that rate) plus $99 a month for maintenance of those rules. The buttons Monthly, Annually (save 2 months) and Apply coupon are on the page, and a banner says You are using a development store, you won't be charged. Differences from the dossier: the dossier lists a Lite plan at $9.99 and a Pro plan at $25.99; the app showed no Lite plan and no Pro at $25.99 (the listing shows $25.99 for Shopify Plus). The app shows one paid plan, Pro at $9.99 on our Shopify Basic development store, and a Custom plan. The dossier question whether Lite includes priority support does not apply: Free has email support and Pro has priority support. Checkout: Upgrade on Pro opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge, the plan Pro Basic, $9,99 USD every 30 days, a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov, subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, total $9,99 due 24 Nov, an Add payment method row and an Approve button. Because a payment method row was on the screen, we pressed Cancel and did not approve; no card was entered and the Free plan stayed active. Cancelling: no subscription was taken. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Smarty Discounts, the menu with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall. The dialog Uninstall Smarty Discounts? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Reason for uninstalling) and Testing multiple apps was chosen. Not tested: the discount in a cart or checkout (the store has a password), the dollar cap, tiers by weight, Buy X Get Y (shown as Test mode required and Pro), time periods, the theme link with Activate for the app embed, approving the test subscription, email support and priority support and their speed. Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps at about 15:3x and the installed list no longer showed it. Other apps were not touched. All our own browser tabs were closed. No theme change was made and no test files were used. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The discount was not tried in a cart, the dossier plans Lite at $9.99 and Pro at $25.99 are not in the app (it shows Free, Pro at $9.99 and Custom at $99), the listing prices change with the Shopify plan of the store, the Custom plan charges $120 an hour for each custom rule, and the Pro approval screen carried an Add payment method row, so we cancelled it.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. Nothing was paid and no theme change was made. Install: the App Store listing (English) is Smarty Discounts by Neezon, rated 5.0 from 6 reviews, with the line Free plan available. Free trial available. The install form was submitted at 15:33:34 and the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked. The app (version 2.7.1) opened straight on the Free plan without a plan or approval screen; a welcome dialog Welcome to Smarty Discounts with 4 steps was dismissed. No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. Core action, a volume discount on products: Create discount, Amount off product, the method Automatic discount, the title Snowboard volume deal, Percentage, Add tier gave Volume-based on Quantity with Tier 1 (Quantity 2, Get 10.0 %) and Add another tier gave Tier 2 (Quantity 4, Get 20.0 %); both are default values and were not changed.
